notes.claim: The column space is all combinations of the columns of A, and the null space is all solutions x of Ax = 0.
The rank of A is the number of independent columns, which equals the number of independent rows.
If b is not in the column space of A, Ax = b has no solution; if the null space holds more than the zero arrow, a solution that exists is not alone.
When rank(A) is less than the number of unknowns n and a solution exists, the solutions form a shifted copy of the null space of dimension n minus the rank.
